name: rapidata
description:
Rapidata brings real human judgment into your AI workflows. Ask a crowd of human annotators to classify items (pick one option per item) or compare two options head-to-head, and get clean, aggregated results back — all from your conversation.

Describe the task in natural language and Claude drafts it and shows you the cost up front. Nothing is collected or charged until you explicitly confirm. Tasks run on Rapidata's global audience, so they start collecting immediately, and results stream back as they come in.

Free to try: billing is pre-paid, pay-as-you-go, and new sign-ups get $20 in free credit — enough to run real tasks end to end at no cost.

Typical uses: evaluating or A/B-testing model outputs, building human-preference and eval datasets, image/text moderation, and settling any question that needs a genuine human answer. For advanced needs — more task types, custom or targeted audiences, and benchmarks — the full Rapidata SDK picks up where these tools leave off.

protocolMetadata.instructions:
Rapidata runs human-in-the-loop labeling tasks. These tools are a small, curated subset of the Rapidata platform: classification and comparison on the global audience, created as a draft and run only after you confirm the cost with the user (creating never spends; start_job does).

Billing is pre-paid, pay-as-you-go for individual (non-organization) accounts, and new sign-ups get $20 in free credit — so trying these tools out is free.

For anything beyond that — other task types (ranking, draw, locate, free text, select words), curated or custom audiences and targeting filters (country, language, age, device), benchmarks/leaderboards, or richer per-annotator results — use the full Rapidata Python SDK directly instead of these tools. The easiest way is to install the official Rapidata skill, which teaches the agent to write Rapidata SDK code: in Claude Code run `/install-plugin https://github.com/RapidataAI/skills`; for other agents see https://docs.rapidata.ai/ai_agents/ . SDK docs: https://docs.rapidata.ai/

tool.title: Create classification task
tool.description:
Create a classification task where humans pick one answer option per item.

        Creates a DRAFT job definition and does NOT start collecting responses (or
        spend): it returns ``confirmation_required`` and expects you to confirm the
        cost with the user, then call ``start_job``. When run, the task goes to the
        global audience (no targeting).

tool.name: create_comparison_task
tool.title: Create comparison task
tool.description:
Create a pairwise comparison task: humans choose between two items each.

        Useful for evaluating or ranking outputs (e.g. which of two images better
        matches a prompt). Like classification, it creates a DRAFT job definition
        and only spends once you confirm the cost with the user and call
        ``start_job``. Each pair must hold exactly two publicly reachable URLs, so
        (unlike classification) the media is required. When run, it goes to the
        global audience.

tool.name: get_job_results
tool.title: Get job results
tool.description:
Fetch results for a job. Never blocks on a still-running job.

        If the job has finished, returns the final results with ``result_status:
        "complete"``; if it was paused, returns the partial snapshot collected so
        far. If it is still processing, returns a ``result_status`` to poll on
        (e.g. ``not_started``, ``collecting``, ``manual_review``) and no results.

_published_faq.name: How do I add rapidata to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add rapidata to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.rapidata.ai/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: Is rapidata MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 14, 2026, rapidata scores 100/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is rapidata's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 14, 2026, rapidata scores 82/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 7 of 7 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the rapidata MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: rapidata provides these MCP tools: create_classification_task, create_comparison_task, get_job_results, get_job_status, list_jobs, pause_job, and start_job.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to rapidata?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to rapidata in data-analytics on the Manufact MCP catalog include Epicure, Newsflash, Point Topic, Pricing Optimizer AI, and StatCite.
rapidata requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.

_published_faq.name: How can rapidata improve its MCP documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: pause_job is the lowest-scoring reviewed tool at 73/100. Declare the result fields and their types in the output schema. Open its review for feedback and a copyable fix prompt, then rerun the documentation review after updating your tool metadata.
rapidata is developed by Rapidata. It is listed as community on the Claude connector directory.
